gallery.description:
True-colour photograph of the Shish Mahal [alt. spelt as 'Sheesh Mahal'] of Lahore Fort, Lahore, Punjab, taken by Stéphane Passet, circa 10–15 January 1914. 
To the left is the Ath Dara, a pavilion was erected by Maharaja Ranjit Singh and served as a public court, beside his private quarters in Sheesh Mahal, Lahore. Its name, Ath Dara, stemmed from the pavilion's eight openings.

gallery.filename: Photograph captioned 'Scene of the transfer of the sovereignty of the Punjab to the British Government; 29th March, 1849.', the Shish Mahal of the Lahore Fort, where the Sikh Empire was formally annexed.jpg
gallery.title: File:Photograph captioned 'Scene of the transfer of the sovereignty of the Punjab to the British Government; 29th March, 1849.', the Shish Mahal of the Lahore Fort, where the Sikh Empire was formally annexed.jpg
gallery.credit: Shared by Gurmanas Singh via Facebook, see: [2]
gallery.source: Photograph captioned 'Scene of the transfer of the sovereignty of the Punjab to the British Government; 29th March, 1849.', the Shish Mahal of the Lahore Fort, where the Sikh Empire was formally annexed
gallery.description:
Photograph captioned 'Scene of the transfer of the sovereignty of the Punjab to the British Government; 29th March, 1849.', the Shish Mahal [alt. spelt as 'Sheesh Mahal'] of the Lahore Fort, where the Sikh Empire was formally/finally annexed on 29 March 1849. A European (possibly British) man can be seen standing near the entryway in the court-yard.
During the reign of the Sikh Empire, the structured and court used to be filled-up with darbaris (officials) and other people of the Lahore Darbar (government/administration of the Sikh Empire/Lahore State] but it laid empty at the time of this post-annexation photograph.
To the left is part of the Ath Dara, a pavilion was erected by Maharaja Ranjit Singh and served as a public court, beside his private quarters in Sheesh Mahal, Lahore. Its name, Ath Dara, stemmed from the pavilion's eight openings.

Further reading on the Ath Dara pavilion: [1]
gallery.dateCreated: circa late 19th or early 20th century (likely ca.1890–1920)
